stances.claim: With help from USAID, American Bar Association, The Asia Foundation, and Asian Development Bank, the Supreme Court recently launched a new, system-wide but rifle-focused reform project nicknamed 'Hustisyeah' -- immediate aim to reduce docket congestion and ultimately speed up dispensation of justice in trial courts.

The dockets of our courts are congested -- this is the sad fact. There are four general causes of case congestion: (1) delay in the adjudication process (protracted/piecemeal trials + dilatory lawyer tactics + lack of investigator-prosecutor coordination in criminal cases + inefficient case buildup); (2) lack of efficient case management system + insufficient management training for judges (addressed separately by eCourt, per CJP June 23 2013 column); (3) uneven distribution of caseloads -- some trial courts have the ideal load of 300, but most are burdened with thousands; (4) lack of accountability -- no effective monitoring system + lack of incentives for judges to reduce caseloads.

Examples: MeTC Branch 80 Muntinlupa and RTC Branch 19 Cavite -- over 3,500 cases each, 'simply impossible to handle.' NCR-MeTC over 2,000 cases: Branch 79 Las Piñas, Branch 63 Makati, Branches 32/34 Quezon City, Branch 81 Valenzuela. Over 1,500 cases: MeTC Branches 68/69/71/72 Pasig + Branches 35/39 Quezon City. Most provincial courts have lighter loads but several over 1,500 (RTC Bulacan + Cavite + Laguna + Antipolo + Iloilo + Cebu + Saranggani + MeTC Lapu-Lapu). Rule-of-thumb: trial court deemed congested above 500.

Hustisyeah is not 'one-size-fits-all' but required each of the 175 target courts to individually inventory their pending cases and identify easily-removable cases without need to hear the parties -- 'moto proprio' dismissable include: outside-jurisdiction + prescribed/out-of-time + no pretrial brief + no pretrial appearance + no discovery + complainant failed to prosecute over unreasonable time. Criminal cases archive: 6-month unserved arrest warrants + accused of unsound mind + jumped bail before arraignment + cannot be arrested after due diligence. Civil cases archive: settled out of court + TROed by higher courts + defendant cannot be served with summons within 6 months (without plaintiff fault). Other clearance: mediation, arbitration, plea bargaining.

These mechanics are not easy to implement, especially for really-congested courts where judges hear cases morning-and-afternoon and write decisions between trials. Paralegals and law students will have to be trained and deployed to help -- typologize cases, identify dismissals/archives, prepare case briefs. The Supreme Court (through OCA) needs to produce easy-to-comprehend manuals and modules to train them.
Once properly and doggedly implemented, Hustisyeah and eCourt can decongest the dockets and speed up the delivery of justice in the trial courts.

notable_anecdotes: The Hustisyeah portmanteau itself -- combining 'hustisya' (justice) with the English 'yeah' affirmation, an unusually playful program-naming for a serious docket-decongestion initiative, here introduced as an SC nickname.
The 'believe it or not' aside -- MeTC Branch 80 Muntinlupa and RTC Branch 19 Cavite each with over 3,500 cases -- a rare CJP rhetorical-flourish in an otherwise data-heavy passage.
The 'rifle-focused' descriptor -- distinguishing Hustisyeah from broad-brush judicial reforms; a precision-metaphor that captures the targeted-court (175-court) approach.
The 300-ideal / 500-rule-of-thumb-congestion / 1,500+ / 2,000+ / 3,500+ caseload tiers -- a tight quantitative ladder that grounds the diagnosis.
The morning-and-afternoon hearings + decision-writing-between-trials judge-day depiction -- a humane realism aside acknowledging why mechanics aren't easy.

The paralegals-and-law-students deployment recommendation -- among CJP's relatively-rare endorsements of law-student-utilization in court administration, signaling Hustisyeah's pragmatic-not-pristine approach.
The properly-and-doggedly closing -- a doubled-adverb closing-condition register that CJP uses sparingly to signal genuine implementation-anxiety beneath endorsement.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban introduces 'Hustisyeah' -- the Supreme Court's recent system-wide but 'rifle-focused' reform project, launched with help from USAID, the American Bar Association, The Asia Foundation, and the Asian Development Bank -- whose immediate aim is to reduce docket congestion and ultimately speed up the dispensation of justice in trial courts. The dockets are congested; the accumulation of prior years' cases aggravated by new filings without corresponding disposition simply produces a huge backlog. Four general causes: (1) delay in adjudication -- protracted/piecemeal trials + dilatory lawyer tactics + lack of investigator-prosecutor coordination in criminal cases (the bulk of congestion) + inefficient case buildup; (2) lack of efficient case management + insufficient management training for judges (addressed separately by eCourt -- see CJP June 23 2013 'Automating the judiciary'); (3) uneven caseload distribution -- some courts have the ideal 300, but most are burdened with thousands. Extreme examples: MeTC Branch 80 Muntinlupa and RTC Branch 19 Cavite each have, 'believe it or not,' over 3,500 cases -- simply impossible to handle. NCR-MeTC branches with over 2,000: Branch 79 Las Piñas, Branch 63 Makati, Branches 32 and 34 Quezon City, Branch 81 Valenzuela; with over 1,500: Branches 68/69/71/72 Pasig and Branches 35/39 Quezon City. Provincial-RTC over 1,500: Branch 16 Bulacan, Branches 89/20/22/23 Cavite, Branches 24/25/93 Laguna, Branches 71/73/74 Antipolo, Branches 66/68 Iloilo, Branches 25/26/53/55/56/60/61 Cebu, Branch 38 Saranggani, MeTC Lapu-Lapu. The rule of thumb: a trial court is congested above 500. (4) Lack of accountability -- no effective monitoring + no judge-incentives. Hustisyeah is not 'one-size-fits-all'; it requires each of the 175 target courts to individually inventory pending cases and identify those easily removable without hearing parties -- 'moto proprio' dismissable: outside-jurisdiction, prescribed/out-of-time, no pretrial brief or appearance, no discovery compliance, or failure-to-prosecute. Criminal cases archive: 6-month unserved arrest warrants, accused of unsound mind, jumped bail before arraignment, un-arrestable despite police due diligence. Civil cases archive: settled out of court, TROed by higher courts, defendant un-servable with summons within 6 months (without plaintiff fault). Other immediate clearance: mediation, arbitration, plea-bargaining agreements not contrary to law or public policy. These mechanics are not easy -- especially for really-congested courts where judges hear cases morning and afternoon and write decisions between trials. Paralegals and law students must be trained and deployed to typologize cases, identify dismissals/archives, prepare case briefs; the SC (through the OCA) needs easy-to-comprehend manuals and modules. Once properly and doggedly implemented, Hustisyeah and eCourt can together decongest the dockets and speed up the delivery of justice in the trial courts.
